key_insight: iFeST iteratively combines frequency, spatial, and temporal modeling to correct fetal brain diffusion MRI motion and improve microstructural reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This medical-imaging framework, rather than a materials-science method, addresses both within-slice corruption and between-slice misalignment.
method: Integrate information across diffusion directions into fiber orientation distributions (FODs).
Use FODs as microstructural priors for intra-slice restoration and inter-slice alignment at the next iteration.
Train using a fetal brain dMRI simulator that synthesizes compound motion artifacts from FODs.
evidence_signal: Simulated evaluations outperformed four inter-slice networks in motion estimation and three intra-slice networks in restoration; real-world validation showed significantly better volume reconstruction and FOD estimation than conventional pipelines.
watch_item: Generalization across scanners and acquisition protocols remains unclear from the abstract, which provides no dataset sizes or numerical effect sizes.
paper_title: iFeST: An Iterative Motion Correction Framework for Fetal Brain Diffusion MRI via Frequency-Spatial-Temporal Modeling
